panels.title: tRPC procedure latency (p95)
panels.description: 95th percentile execution time per tRPC procedure, parsed from the app's own "[TRPC] <procedure> took <n>ms to execute" lines. This is the submitter's main path to Mongo, so it is the earliest signal that a query has regressed.

targets.expr: quantile_over_time(0.95, {job="chill-subs-dev", process="chillest-subs"} | regexp `\[TRPC\] (?P<proc>[^ ]+) took (?P<ms>[0-9]+)ms` | unwrap ms [$__rate_interval]) by (proc)

panels.title: tRPC call rate by procedure
panels.description: Calls per second per procedure. Read alongside the latency panel: a procedure that is both hot and slow is the one worth optimising.

targets.expr: sum by (proc) (rate({job="chill-subs-dev", process="chillest-subs"} | regexp `\[TRPC\] (?P<proc>[^ ]+) took (?P<ms>[0-9]+)ms` | proc != `` [$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: HTTP responses by status
panels.description: Next.js request log for the submitter, parsed from "GET /path 200 in 123ms". The label filter after the regexp is deliberate: without it every non-request line would be counted too.

targets.expr: sum by (status) (rate({job="chill-subs-dev", process="chillest-subs"} | regexp `(?P<method>GET|POST|PUT|PATCH|DELETE) (?P<path>[^ ]+) (?P<status>[0-9]{3}) in (?P<ms>[0-9]+)ms` | status =~ `[0-9]+` [$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: HTTP request duration
panels.description: End-to-end request time as Next.js reports it, p95 and max. In dev this includes on-demand compilation, so first hits on a cold route are expected to be slow.

targets.expr: quantile_over_time(0.95, {job="chill-subs-dev", process="chillest-subs"} | regexp `(?P<method>GET|POST|PUT|PATCH|DELETE) (?P<path>[^ ]+) (?P<status>[0-9]{3}) in (?P<ms>[0-9]+)ms` | status =~ `[0-9]+` | unwrap ms [$__rate_interval]) by ()

max_over_time({job="chill-subs-dev", process="chillest-subs"} | regexp `(?P<method>GET|POST|PUT|PATCH|DELETE) (?P<path>[^ ]+) (?P<status>[0-9]{3}) in (?P<ms>[0-9]+)ms` | status =~ `[0-9]+` | unwrap ms [$__rate_interval]) by ()

panels.title: editor route compile time
panels.description: Next.js dev compilation per route, from "✓ Compiled /route in 882ms". Climbing numbers here are what a slow edit-refresh loop actually feels like.

targets.expr: max_over_time({job="chill-subs-dev", process="editor"} | regexp `Compiled (?P<route>[^ ]+) in (?P<ms>[0-9]+)ms` | unwrap ms [$__rate_interval]) by (route)

panels.title: Typesense index size by collection
panels.description: Documents pulled from Mongo per reindex pass, per collection, from "<collection> fetched <n>, attempted <n>". This is the Mongo -> Typesense pipeline that makes editor listings searchable in the submitter; a collection dropping to zero means the submitter has stopped finding those records.

targets.expr: max_over_time({job="chill-subs-dev", process="typesense-indexer"} | regexp `\] (?P<collection>[a-z ]+) fetched (?P<docs>[0-9]+), attempted` | unwrap docs [$__rate_interval]) by (collection)

panels.title: Slowest calls and requests
panels.description: Raw tRPC and HTTP timing lines from the submitter, newest first — the detail behind the latency panels. Galley's backend is absent by design: it exposes no /metrics endpoint and logs nothing at its default level, so set RUST_LOG to get request telemetry from it.
